- Following changes i made in `spark-perf-master/config/config.py` file. SPARK_HOME_DIR = `"/home/test/spark-1.5.1"` RUN_SPARK_TESTS = `False` RUN_PYSPARK_TESTS =`False` RUN_STREAMING_TESTS =`False` RUN_MLLIB_TESTS = `False` RUN_PYTHON_MLLIB_TESTS = `True` PREP_SPARK_TESTS = `False` PREP_PYSPARK_TESTS = `False` PREP_STREAMING_TESTS =` False` PREP_MLLIB_TESTS = `False` COMMON_JAVA_OPTS = `[ JavaOptionSet("spark.storage.memoryFraction", [2]), JavaOptionSet("spark.serializer", ["org.apache.spark.serializer.JavaSerializer"]), JavaOptionSet("spark.executor.memory", ["18g"]), JavaOptionSet("spark.locality.wait", [str(60 * 1000 * 1000)]) ]` SPARK_DRIVER_MEMORY = `"20g"` MLLIB_SPARK_VERSION = `1.5`
- Is this a bug in `spark-perf`? A problem with Spark 1.5.1? I'm trying to figure out if this issue is actionable.
- Exactly not able to figure out, but i think it's not problem with `spark 1.5.1.`, because we can get output for other `SPARK_TESTS` entry in `spark-perf-master/config/config.py`
- Even we tried `spark-perf` with `spark 1.5.2` getting same issue `java.io.IOException (No space left on device)` for `RUN_PYTHON_MLLIB_TESTS = True`
- I see this outside spark-perf. in Spark 1.5.0. Something similar was reported in [July](http://comments.gmane.org/gmane.comp.lang.scala.spark.user/15910) for Spark 1.3.
- so @username_2 @username_1 i think it might be bug in `spark-perf`. Please take this issue on action.
- @username_0 Can you try running a problem of similar size outside of Spark perf, but on the same cluster and with a similar configuration? Also, are you running with only 1 worker with 16GB of memory, and if so, does it work if you add a few more workers?
- @username_3 We got output for `RUN_MLLIB_TESTS = True` with same cluster and with a similar configuration but for `RUN_PYTHON_MLLIB_TESTS = True` getting above issue. As well till now we tried 1 worker with 24GB of memory (max) not with more workers.
- I see. I'm still not sure if it's a problem with spark-perf or with pyspark requiring more memory than equivalent Scala/Java jobs. The best way to figure that out might be to try to replicate the ML task outside of spark-perf. I wouldn't call this a fix, but one thing you could try is lowering the number of partitions. For ML jobs, I tend to set # partitions = # CPU cores available in cluster. That will likely mean less memory allocated.
- @username_3 where we need to do that configuration changes..? Plz can you explain little more with small example...?
- This can be set in the spark-perf/config/config.py file. Note that there is an mllib-specific num-partitions config in that file.

Title:
converting fasta to adam eats a huge ammount of time and memory

Description:
I wonder why I need >15GB RAM and >1 hour time with 8 cores just to convert some 800MB fasta file to ADAM format? Crazy memory and CPU consumption of ADAM's FastaConverter makes ADAM unusable in many use-cases. What is also annoying is that when it lakes memory it often continues for ages instead of just crashing

Comments:
- Hi @username_0! Is this a standard reference genome that you could share? By any chance, is it gzipped? Our FASTA converter is not particularly zippy, but the runtimes you are describing seem extremely slow.
- @username_1 yes, super-slow and often freezing conversions are a big pain for me and the reason why I use ADAM not as often as I would want to. I have no idea what is wrong there :( Here is the latest example of frozen conversion: I converted this 500mb not gziped file http://agingkills.westeurope.cloudapp.azure.com/pipelines/indexes/BOWHEAD_WHALE/Alaska/Trinity.fasta to adam format. I uploaded it to HDFS and ran the following command: ``` ./convert.sh alaska/Trinity.fasta alaska/transcripts.adam 8G 4 ``` where convert.sh is just: ``` #!/bin/bash docker run --network=bigdata_default -p 4040:4040 quay.io/comp-bio-aging/adam:latest /opt/adam/bin/adam-submit \ --master spark://spark-master:7077 --executor-memory $3 --total-executor-cores $4 --driver-memory 5G -- \ fasta2adam hdfs://namenode/pipelines/BOWHEAD_WHALE/$1 hdfs://namenode/pipelines/BOWHEAD_WHALE/$2 ``` My bigdata containers are at ( https://github.com/username_0/bigdata-docker/tree/master/containers ), including adam one https://github.com/username_0/bigdata-docker/blob/master/containers/adam/Dockerfile . The spark configuration was https://github.com/username_0/bigdata-docker/blob/master/conf/spark/master.conf I ran it at two nodes cluster with 30GB RAM per node. I uploaded fasta file to HDFS. As it was a bit more than 500MB I gave only 8GB RAM to the job. The job was running for 2.4 hours and I had to stop it. Title:
converting fasta to adam eats a huge ammount of time and memory

Description:
I wonder why I need >15GB RAM and >1 hour time with 8 cores just to convert some 800MB fasta file to ADAM format? Crazy memory and CPU consumption of ADAM's FastaConverter makes ADAM unusable in many use-cases. What is also annoying is that when it lakes memory it often continues for ages instead of just crashing

Title:
converting fasta to adam eats a huge ammount of time and memory

Description:
I wonder why I need >15GB RAM and >1 hour time with 8 cores just to convert some 800MB fasta file to ADAM format? Crazy memory and CPU consumption of ADAM's FastaConverter makes ADAM unusable in many use-cases. What is also annoying is that when it lakes memory it often continues for ages instead of just crashing

Title:
converting fasta to adam eats a huge ammount of time and memory

Description:
I wonder why I need >15GB RAM and >1 hour time with 8 cores just to convert some 800MB fasta file to ADAM format? Crazy memory and CPU consumption of ADAM's FastaConverter makes ADAM unusable in many use-cases. What is also annoying is that when it lakes memory it often continues for ages instead of just crashing

Title:
converting fasta to adam eats a huge ammount of time and memory

Description:
I wonder why I need >15GB RAM and >1 hour time with 8 cores just to convert some 800MB fasta file to ADAM format? Crazy memory and CPU consumption of ADAM's FastaConverter makes ADAM unusable in many use-cases. What is also annoying is that when it lakes memory it often continues for ages instead of just crashing

Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Note that there is nothing special about the collect function: the job has gotten stuck on other tasks and the job has also been stuck when this page shows nothing is running at all. ![shot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699998-64515480-78ca-11ea-950a-cd4b4b399bb2.png) In this screenshot, we see the status of the executors during the stuck state. From this page, we can see that nothing is in fact running. This is typical during everytime the job has gotten stuck. Note that this screenshot was taken at the same time as the previous one: so while one page shows a job is active, another shows it cannot be so. ![shot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699997-63202780-78ca-11ea-9a7f-2198259982f0.png) And this screenshot is what it looks like from the R session (I've blotted out the model names that were printed). Note that after a considerable amount of time, and after I took the above screenshots, I hit Ctrl+C and tried to view some of the data that was made by running "selectedData". This action was not logged, no data was ever printed, and the above screenshots stayed the same. There is also nothing special about the job getting stuck after it prints "Data quantiled", it has gotten stuck after it printed out "Data selected" on the exact same model, as well as in various other places on this and other models. Again, if I run model 7 all by itself, it finishes just fine: the code is correct to the best of my knowledge. ![shot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699990-61566400-78ca-11ea-9431-049ff27908e2.png) I've tried everything I can think of: I've reversed the order that the models are executed in, I've increased the memory, I've increased the timeouts, I've decreased those configurations.

Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Note that there is nothing special about the collect function: the job has gotten stuck on other tasks and the job has also been stuck when this page shows nothing is running at all. ![shot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699998-64515480-78ca-11ea-950a-cd4b4b399bb2.png) In this screenshot, we see the status of the executors during the stuck state. From this page, we can see that nothing is in fact running. This is typical during everytime the job has gotten stuck. Note that this screenshot was taken at the same time as the previous one: so while one page shows a job is active, another shows it cannot be so. ![shot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699997-63202780-78ca-11ea-9a7f-2198259982f0.png) And this screenshot is what it looks like from the R session (I've blotted out the model names that were printed). Note that after a considerable amount of time, and after I took the above screenshots, I hit Ctrl+C and tried to view some of the data that was made by running "selectedData". This action was not logged, no data was ever printed, and the above screenshots stayed the same. There is also nothing special about the job getting stuck after it prints "Data quantiled", it has gotten stuck after it printed out "Data selected" on the exact same model, as well as in various other places on this and other models. Again, if I run model 7 all by itself, it finishes just fine: the code is correct to the best of my knowledge. ![shot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699990-61566400-78ca-11ea-9431-049ff27908e2.png) I've tried everything I can think of: I've reversed the order that the models are executed in, I've increased the memory, I've increased the timeouts, I've decreased those configurations.

Comments:

- @username_0 Here are a couple thoughts... 1. Does your `core-site.xml` have the following lines (or something similar) per this [stack overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/17265002/hadoop-no-filesystem-for-scheme-file)? ``` <property> <name>fs.file.impl</name> <value>org.apache.hadoop.fs.LocalFileSystem</value> <description>The FileSystem for file: uris.</description> </property> <property> <name>fs.hdfs.impl</name> <value>org.apache.hadoop.hdfs.DistributedFileSystem</value> <description>The FileSystem for hdfs: uris.</description> </property> ``` 2. I see you're using `--conf spark.executorEnv.CLASSPATH="$($HADOOP_HOME/bin/hadoop classpath --glob):${CLASSPATH}"` which sets the executor's classpath to the `hadoop classpath` of your gateway/launcher box. This is hopefully the same as your grid nodes. 3. Just to be sure, you may want to dump the `CLASSPATH` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (and maybe `$(hadoop classpath --glob)` as seen by the executors (i.e. inside the TF code), just to see if there's anything unexpected.

Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Note that there is nothing special about the collect function: the job has gotten stuck on other tasks and the job has also been stuck when this page shows nothing is running at all. ![shot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699998-64515480-78ca-11ea-950a-cd4b4b399bb2.png) In this screenshot, we see the status of the executors during the stuck state. From this page, we can see that nothing is in fact running. This is typical during everytime the job has gotten stuck. Note that this screenshot was taken at the same time as the previous one: so while one page shows a job is active, another shows it cannot be so. ![shot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699997-63202780-78ca-11ea-9a7f-2198259982f0.png) And this screenshot is what it looks like from the R session (I've blotted out the model names that were printed). Note that after a considerable amount of time, and after I took the above screenshots, I hit Ctrl+C and tried to view some of the data that was made by running "selectedData". This action was not logged, no data was ever printed, and the above screenshots stayed the same. There is also nothing special about the job getting stuck after it prints "Data quantiled", it has gotten stuck after it printed out "Data selected" on the exact same model, as well as in various other places on this and other models. Again, if I run model 7 all by itself, it finishes just fine: the code is correct to the best of my knowledge. ![shot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699990-61566400-78ca-11ea-9431-049ff27908e2.png) I've tried everything I can think of: I've reversed the order that the models are executed in, I've increased the memory, I've increased the timeouts, I've decreased those configurations.

Comments:

Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Note that there is nothing special about the collect function: the job has gotten stuck on other tasks and the job has also been stuck when this page shows nothing is running at all. ![shot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699998-64515480-78ca-11ea-950a-cd4b4b399bb2.png) In this screenshot, we see the status of the executors during the stuck state. From this page, we can see that nothing is in fact running. This is typical during everytime the job has gotten stuck. Note that this screenshot was taken at the same time as the previous one: so while one page shows a job is active, another shows it cannot be so. ![shot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699997-63202780-78ca-11ea-9a7f-2198259982f0.png) And this screenshot is what it looks like from the R session (I've blotted out the model names that were printed). Note that after a considerable amount of time, and after I took the above screenshots, I hit Ctrl+C and tried to view some of the data that was made by running "selectedData". This action was not logged, no data was ever printed, and the above screenshots stayed the same. There is also nothing special about the job getting stuck after it prints "Data quantiled", it has gotten stuck after it printed out "Data selected" on the exact same model, as well as in various other places on this and other models. Again, if I run model 7 all by itself, it finishes just fine: the code is correct to the best of my knowledge. ![shot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699990-61566400-78ca-11ea-9431-049ff27908e2.png) I've tried everything I can think of: I've reversed the order that the models are executed in, I've increased the memory, I've increased the timeouts, I've decreased those configurations.

Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Note that there is nothing special about the collect function: the job has gotten stuck on other tasks and the job has also been stuck when this page shows nothing is running at all. ![shot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699998-64515480-78ca-11ea-950a-cd4b4b399bb2.png) In this screenshot, we see the status of the executors during the stuck state. From this page, we can see that nothing is in fact running. This is typical during everytime the job has gotten stuck. Note that this screenshot was taken at the same time as the previous one: so while one page shows a job is active, another shows it cannot be so. ![shot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699997-63202780-78ca-11ea-9a7f-2198259982f0.png) And this screenshot is what it looks like from the R session (I've blotted out the model names that were printed). Note that after a considerable amount of time, and after I took the above screenshots, I hit Ctrl+C and tried to view some of the data that was made by running "selectedData". This action was not logged, no data was ever printed, and the above screenshots stayed the same. There is also nothing special about the job getting stuck after it prints "Data quantiled", it has gotten stuck after it printed out "Data selected" on the exact same model, as well as in various other places on this and other models. Again, if I run model 7 all by itself, it finishes just fine: the code is correct to the best of my knowledge. ![shot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699990-61566400-78ca-11ea-9431-049ff27908e2.png) I've tried everything I can think of: I've reversed the order that the models are executed in, I've increased the memory, I've increased the timeouts, I've decreased those configurations.

Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Note that there is nothing special about the collect function: the job has gotten stuck on other tasks and the job has also been stuck when this page shows nothing is running at all. ![shot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699998-64515480-78ca-11ea-950a-cd4b4b399bb2.png) In this screenshot, we see the status of the executors during the stuck state. From this page, we can see that nothing is in fact running. This is typical during everytime the job has gotten stuck. Note that this screenshot was taken at the same time as the previous one: so while one page shows a job is active, another shows it cannot be so. ![shot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699997-63202780-78ca-11ea-9a7f-2198259982f0.png) And this screenshot is what it looks like from the R session (I've blotted out the model names that were printed). Note that after a considerable amount of time, and after I took the above screenshots, I hit Ctrl+C and tried to view some of the data that was made by running "selectedData". This action was not logged, no data was ever printed, and the above screenshots stayed the same. There is also nothing special about the job getting stuck after it prints "Data quantiled", it has gotten stuck after it printed out "Data selected" on the exact same model, as well as in various other places on this and other models. Again, if I run model 7 all by itself, it finishes just fine: the code is correct to the best of my knowledge. ![shot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699990-61566400-78ca-11ea-9431-049ff27908e2.png) I've tried everything I can think of: I've reversed the order that the models are executed in, I've increased the memory, I've increased the timeouts, I've decreased those configurations.

Comments:

Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Note that there is nothing special about the collect function: the job has gotten stuck on other tasks and the job has also been stuck when this page shows nothing is running at all. ![shot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699998-64515480-78ca-11ea-950a-cd4b4b399bb2.png) In this screenshot, we see the status of the executors during the stuck state. From this page, we can see that nothing is in fact running. This is typical during everytime the job has gotten stuck. Note that this screenshot was taken at the same time as the previous one: so while one page shows a job is active, another shows it cannot be so. ![shot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699997-63202780-78ca-11ea-9a7f-2198259982f0.png) And this screenshot is what it looks like from the R session (I've blotted out the model names that were printed). Note that after a considerable amount of time, and after I took the above screenshots, I hit Ctrl+C and tried to view some of the data that was made by running "selectedData". This action was not logged, no data was ever printed, and the above screenshots stayed the same. There is also nothing special about the job getting stuck after it prints "Data quantiled", it has gotten stuck after it printed out "Data selected" on the exact same model, as well as in various other places on this and other models. Again, if I run model 7 all by itself, it finishes just fine: the code is correct to the best of my knowledge. ![shot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699990-61566400-78ca-11ea-9431-049ff27908e2.png) I've tried everything I can think of: I've reversed the order that the models are executed in, I've increased the memory, I've increased the timeouts, I've decreased those configurations.

Title:
Job freezes for no apparent reason

Description:
I have a job that gets stuck part way through it. And by stuck I mean like frozen, as if time itself stopped. The job is basically a scoring job: I have several R models that I want to score. The code for each model is encapsulated in its own R file. I have a wrapper that runs them one after the other and they all share the same spark connection. Unfortunately, in the middle of the job, around the 5th, 6th, or 7th model, the job freezes (where exactly seems nondeterministic but in roughly the same spot). There are no error messages and there is nothing in the log that indicates what the problem might be. The code freezes at roughly the same point each time, but when I run just that model by itself in its own spark job, it runs just fine. I have tried numerous things to determine if the problem is in my code, but I believe the problem is environmental, or with sparklyr/spark, not with the code I am running. To fully reproduce this, I would have to provide proprietary data which I cannot do, but I'm going to take a shot at providing a skeleton that you could theoretically use to reconstruct the issue. There are six sets of files of interest: 1. The R code that runs the whole job (called "code wrapper.R") 2. The R code that scores each model (called "model1.R", "model2.R", etc.) 3. The RDS files that contain each model (these are caret models, and the files are called "model1.RDS", "model2.RDS", etc.) 4. The json files that describe the layout needed for each model (called "model1.json", etc.) 5. The config file for the spark job (called "spark-config.yml") 6. The input data (this is an avro file on hdfs) The input data is fairly small for testing, ~75000 rows and 4000 columns. The 4000 columns are subsetted down to ~50 or so features, so most of the columns are not used (but different columns may be used by each model). The code wrapper basically just does this: ```r spark_version <- "2.4.0" files <- list.files("my_directory", pattern=".R$") # get all the model#.R files isFirstModel <- T isFinalModel <- F for (i in seq(length(files))) { print(i) source(files[i]) #sources, but does not execute, the model scoring if (i %% length(files) == 0) {isFinalModel <- T} executeSpark() # executes what is in model#.R isFirstModel <- F } ``` Each model#.R file is fairly simple in logical construction, as well. It's basically: start spark connection if there isn't one, load the data, do some manipulations and score it, then save it out. I'll omit some of the details (like paths to files), but otherwise this code should be complete. I'll put the code at the end. Below is the configuration that is used in the spark.yml file (I've omitted the URIs since my company doesn't want me to share those, and /mnt/ifs81001 is a drive that is shared by all nodes in the cluster): ```yml # Set spark options below default: spark.master: yarn spark.submit.deployMode: client spark.home: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/ spark.yarn.jars: /opt/ssbe/ssbe-spark/jars/* spark.logConf: true spark.driver.memory: 4g spark.driver.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.executor.memory: 4g spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 4g spark.driver.maxResultSize: 0 spark.executor.cores: 1 spark.yarn.stagingDir: hdfs://namenode:/tmp/ spark.local.dir: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/temp/ spark.shuffle.service.enabled: true spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: true spark.yarn.maxAppAttempts: 2 spark.task.maxFailures: 2 spark.network.timeout: 10000s spark.executor.heartbeatInterval: 30s spark.serializer: org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer spark.r.command: /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/bin/Rscript spark.r.libpaths: - /mnt/ifs81001/dataarch/sbanalyst/miniconda3/envs/my_env/lib/R/library ``` ```r suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(assertthat) library(rlang) library(config) library(rjson) library(caret) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(sparkavro) library(sparklyr) [Truncated] [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_3.6.2 Here are some screenshots: In this screenshot, we see what the job looks like in its "stuck" state. It appears as though the job is running a task, but it isn't. Note that there is nothing special about the collect function: the job has gotten stuck on other tasks and the job has also been stuck when this page shows nothing is running at all. ![shot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699998-64515480-78ca-11ea-950a-cd4b4b399bb2.png) In this screenshot, we see the status of the executors during the stuck state. From this page, we can see that nothing is in fact running. This is typical during everytime the job has gotten stuck. Note that this screenshot was taken at the same time as the previous one: so while one page shows a job is active, another shows it cannot be so. ![shot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699997-63202780-78ca-11ea-9a7f-2198259982f0.png) And this screenshot is what it looks like from the R session (I've blotted out the model names that were printed). Note that after a considerable amount of time, and after I took the above screenshots, I hit Ctrl+C and tried to view some of the data that was made by running "selectedData". This action was not logged, no data was ever printed, and the above screenshots stayed the same. There is also nothing special about the job getting stuck after it prints "Data quantiled", it has gotten stuck after it printed out "Data selected" on the exact same model, as well as in various other places on this and other models. Again, if I run model 7 all by itself, it finishes just fine: the code is correct to the best of my knowledge. ![shot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22136131/78699990-61566400-78ca-11ea-9431-049ff27908e2.png) I've tried everything I can think of: I've reversed the order that the models are executed in, I've increased the memory, I've increased the timeouts, I've decreased those configurations.
